title: backlog.py land takes a host-wide lock for its heavy checks instead of a token passed by message
goal: backlog.py land, and backlog.py done when an item's checks run the full tests.py or stress_test.py, take a host-wide lock (a lock file under the clone's git common dir, naming the holder session, item and start time, released on exit and taken over when its process is gone) before the heavy checks, waiting or refusing with the holder named, so concurrent orchestrators never run two heavy runs at once. Answers SP-x2pvljz6: four sessions passed a land token by message all day, the host ran out of memory once, and a review's done started a full suite without the token.
notes: A lock wait and hold are recorded as ops host.lock rows once the ops sidecar exists.
